title: Predictive Uncertainty with Revised Economic Data
abstract: arXiv:2607.05882v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Data revisions create uncertainty that outlives the first publication of an economic indicator. We develop a framework that turns an existing point forecast of the first release into a predictive distribution for a later release. The framework combines forecast-error records with official-release histories, including periods without recorded forecasts. We establish identification conditions and, from the component distributions, construct sharp bounds for directional probabilities and dependence-robust prediction intervals. We also show when additional revision records strictly improve estimation precision for a fixed rare-tail bound. Monte Carlo simulations quantify the predictive gains from longer release histories. Across four US inflation series, full histories improve interval scores relative to forecast-matched histories, with the largest gains in PCE. translated_title: 基于修正经济数据的预测不确定性
translated_abstract: 数据修正所产生的不确定性在经济指标首次发布之后仍会长期存在。我们开发了一个框架，能够将针对首次发布的现有点预测转换为针对后续修正数据发布的预测分布。该框架将预测误差记录与官方发布历史相结合，其中也包括没有预测记录的时期。我们建立了识别条件，并从各分量分布出发，构建了方向性概率的精确界以及稳健于相依结构的预测区间。我们还证明了在何种条件下，额外的修正记录能够在固定稀有尾部界的前提下严格提高估计精度。蒙特卡洛模拟量化了更长的发布历史所带来的预测收益。在美国四个通胀序列上，使用完整历史相对于仅匹配预测的历史改进了区间得分，其中PCE（个人消费支出价格指数）的收益最大。条件性方法将合并区间得分降低了27-28%……
tldr: 该论文提出了一个将经济指标首次发布的点预测转化为后续修正数据预测分布的框架，并证明完整的官方发布历史能显著提升预测精度，在美国通胀序列上使合并区间得分降低27-28%。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a framework that converts point forecasts of an economic indicator's initial release into predictive distributions for revised data, showing that complete official release histories substantially improve prediction accuracy, reducing pooled interval scores by 27–28% across US inflation series.
